subject.title: Feature: Respect userTimezone in memory file timestamps and naming

question: Should bundled session-memory hook filenames and `# Session` headers use `agents.defaults.userTimezone` rather than the gateway host timezone for existing users?
rationale: Current main and v2026.6.11 have shipped host-local session-memory artifacts, while this issue asks to bind those artifacts to configured user timezone; that changes persisted filenames and user-visible day grouping.

options.title: Use existing userTimezone
options.body: Make the bundled session-memory hook use `agents.defaults.userTimezone` with host fallback, matching memory-core auto-flush behavior and avoiding a new config surface.

options.title: Keep host-local artifacts
options.body: Document and preserve the current session-memory hook contract that artifacts follow the gateway host timezone.

options.title: Add dedicated memory timezone
options.body: Introduce a separate memory artifact timezone only if independent control is worth the extra config, docs, and upgrade burden.

recommendation.title: Use existing userTimezone
recommendation.body: Make the bundled session-memory hook use `agents.defaults.userTimezone` with host fallback, matching memory-core auto-flush behavior and avoiding a new config surface.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged local-timezone repair in this hook is the clearest current-main ownership signal for the remaining compatibility choice.
